Selections of unrelated individuals

Source: R/rkn_selection.R
rkn_selection.Rd

rkn_select_random, rkn_select_criteria and rkn_select_global return an object of class rkn_selection: a list holding the selected individuals, the network they were selected from and, when computed, diagnostics on how each individual and each family was resolved. The object has print, summary and plot methods.

Throughout the package, a maximum set of unrelated individuals is a set with no related pair of the largest possible size: in graph terms, a maximum independent set of the relatedness network. A network usually has many maximum sets, which differ in which individuals they contain; a family is a connected component of the network (see the section Family structures).

Components

kept

character vector, the identifiers of the selected individuals;

discarded

character vector, the identifiers of the other individuals;

family_sizes

integer vector, the size of each family (connected component of the network);

method

"random", "criteria" or "global";

uniform

logical, whether the selection was drawn uniformly among the maximum sets (rkn_select_random(uniform = TRUE));

optimal

logical, whether the criteria were evaluated over all the maximum sets of each family (rkn_select_criteria(optimal = TRUE));

criteria

for criteria-based selections, a list with the primary and, if given, the secondary criterion; NULL otherwise;

seed

the seed of the selection, or NULL;

diagnostics

logical, whether diagnostics were computed;

node_diagnostics

a data frame with one row per individual, or NULL without diagnostics. Columns: id; pre_class, how the individual was decided ("kept_apriori", "discarded_apriori", "candidate_simple" or "candidate_complex", described with their labels in the section Types of decision below); post_class, "kept" or "discarded"; is_selected, the outcome as a logical; pre_reason, an internal label of the rule or procedure that decided the individual; family_id and family_size; in uniform selections, inclusion_probability, the exact probability that the individual is selected, i.e. the proportion of the maximum sets of its family that contain it (NA in the families too intricate for uniform sampling). From these probabilities print() reports the expected number of selected individuals that differ between two independent uniform draws, the sum of \(p(1 - p)\) over the individuals: the part of the selection left to chance;

family_summary

a data frame with one row per family, or NULL without diagnostics. Columns: family_id and family_size; selector, "upto5" for families resolved by the structural rules in rules_db, "6plus" for larger families, "uniform" for families drawn uniformly and "optimal" for families where the criteria were evaluated over all maximum sets; structure_name, an internal label of the recognised structure; mis_method, how the individuals left undecided by the structural rules were resolved (see the section Search over maximum sets): "enumeration", "exact", "exact_reduced" or "exact_sample", or NA when no search was needed because the rules decided every individual or chose among the candidates they identified, as in a related pair; in uniform selections and in selections over all maximum sets, every family is searched; uniform, whether the family was drawn uniformly among its maximum sets; optimal, whether the criteria were evaluated over all its maximum sets; n_max_sets, in the families drawn uniformly or evaluated over all maximum sets, the number of maximum sets of the family (NA otherwise, and after "exact_reduced"; Inf beyond about \(1.8 \times 10^{308}\), the largest number R can store); the numbers of kept and discarded individuals, overall (n_kept, n_discarded) and by type of decision (n_kept_apriori, n_discarded_apriori, n_candidate_simple, n_candidate_complex). Since the choices in different families are independent, the maximum sets of the network are all the combinations of one maximum set per family: their number, reported by print(), is the product of n_max_sets over the families and grows exponentially with the number of families that have a choice (each related pair doubles it), so print() also reports how many families have more than one maximum set. In global selections the columns are family_id, family_size, selector ("global"), exact (FALSE for the families beyond the computational budget, see rkn_select_global), n_kept, n_discarded, n_category (selected members in the category) or, for a numeric covariate, mean (mean of the covariate among the selected members with a known value, NA if none), and n_missing (selected members with a missing value), and the types of decision of node_diagnostics are not available;

graph

the igraph network the selection was made on;

call

the call that produced the selection;

global

for global selections, a list describing the composition reached: type, "proportion" for a categorical covariate or "mean" for a numeric one; covariate and target; cohort, whether the target is the proportion or mean of the network; n_known and n_missing, the selected individuals with a known and a missing value; size, max_size and max_loss; log_count, the natural logarithm of the number of selections reaching the same composition and size (NA when exact is FALSE); exact, whether every family was computed exactly; n_inexact, the number of families that were not. For a categorical covariate, also category, proportion (the proportion reached among the selected individuals with a known value) and n_category; for a numeric covariate, mean (the mean of the recorded values among the selected individuals with a known value), resolution, rounded (whether some value was rounded for the search) and coarsened (whether the default resolution was coarsened to fit the memory and time budgets). NULL otherwise.

Family structures

A family is a connected component of the relatedness network: a group of individuals linked, directly or through other members, by relatedness above the threshold used to build the network. summary.rkn_selection groups the families into seven structures:

single individual

an individual related to no one else in the cohort;

related pair

two related individuals;

chain of three

three individuals of whom two are not related to each other but both are related to the third, typically two parents and their child;

three mutually related

three individuals all related to each other, for instance three siblings or a parent and two children;

family of 4, of 5, and of 6 or more members

larger families. Families of up to 5 members are resolved by the structural rules in rules_db, larger families by reducing the family step by step with structural rules and resolving what remains.

Search over maximum sets

The structural rules decide many individuals directly. The individuals they leave undecided are resolved by a search over the maximum sets of unrelated individuals, reported in the column mis_method of family_summary:

"enumeration"

in families of up to 5 members, all the maximum sets are listed and one of them is chosen;

"exact"

in families of 6 or more members, an exact algorithm (dynamic programming along an elimination ordering of the family) finds the maximum size and draws one of the maximum sets uniformly at random. Its cost grows with how intricate the relationships are, not with the size of the family, so it also handles the large families of genetic isolates;

"exact_reduced"

the same after removing the individuals who cannot enlarge the selection (an individual is removed when one of their relatives has no relative outside their own). This is used only for families too intricate for the exact algorithm: the set chosen is still of maximum size, but not drawn uniformly. In criteria-based selections an individual is removed only if that relative meets the criteria at least as well, so the criteria are still optimised exactly, or, with missing covariate values, evaluated on the maximum sets that remain. If the family is still too intricate, individuals are removed regardless of the criteria, as in selections without criteria: the set is still of maximum size, and the criteria are optimised over the maximum sets that remain.

"exact_sample"

criteria-based selections only: see below.

In criteria-based selections (rkn_select_criteria), the criteria are optimised exactly by the same algorithm when no undecided member of the family lacks the covariate, because among sets of the same size they rank sets by the number of members meeting the condition. When some undecided member lacks it, the score is a proportion among the members with a known value, which the algorithm cannot maximise directly: the criteria are then evaluated on all the maximum sets when there are at most 10,000; above that number, as in some large families of genetic isolates, they are evaluated on a uniform random sample of 10,000 maximum sets, and the best of the sample is kept ("exact_sample"). The number of such families is reported by print(). In uniform selections and in selections over all maximum sets, no structural rule is applied, and every family is searched in this way. If a family remains too intricate even after this reduction, the selection stops with an error that names one of its members and suggests excluding the samples flagged by rkn_check_samples or using a higher threshold, which joins closer relatives only.

Types of decision

Within each family, every individual is decided in one of four ways, reported by summary.rkn_selection and shown by the "diagnostics" plot (see plot.rkn_selection):

kept without a choice ("kept_apriori")

the individual is kept with no alternative to choose from: a rule based on the structure of the family keeps them (for instance the leaves of a star-shaped family), or they belong to every maximum set of the individuals left undecided by the rules;

discarded without a choice ("discarded_apriori")

likewise, the individual is discarded by a structural rule (for instance the centre of a star) or belongs to no maximum set of the individuals left undecided;

decided among single candidates ("candidate_simple")

the remaining choice is among interchangeable candidates of a single group, such as the two members of a related pair, and one of them is selected;

decided among alternative sets ("candidate_complex")

several maximum sets remain that differ in more than one individual, and one of them is selected. These are the sets left by the rules, not necessarily all the maximum sets of the family.

The choices among candidates are made at random by rkn_select_random and by the criteria in rkn_select_criteria.

"Without a choice" describes the procedure, not the family: to simplify the search, the structural rules fix some individuals that other maximum sets of the family leave out (for instance, in a chain of relatives they keep the individual at the end), so an individual kept without a choice is not necessarily in every maximum set of the family. The exact classes over the whole family are given by uniform selections.

In uniform selections (rkn_select_random(uniform = TRUE)) no structural rule is applied, and the same codes have an exact meaning, computed from the inclusion probabilities: "kept_apriori", in every maximum set (probability 1); "discarded_apriori", in no maximum set (probability 0); "candidate_complex", chosen at random among the maximum sets (probability strictly between 0 and 1). summary() and plot() label them accordingly.

In criteria-based selections over all maximum sets (rkn_select_criteria(optimal = TRUE)) no structural rule is applied either: "kept_apriori" and "discarded_apriori" again mean in every and in no maximum set, and "candidate_complex" chosen by the criteria among maximum sets that differ, which summary() and plot() label accordingly.

In both kinds of selection, the families too intricate for the exact computation, whose number print() reports, are selected by the structural rules, and their codes keep the meaning given above for selections with rules. In the families reduced by dominance (mis_method "exact_reduced"), the individuals removed by the reduction count as in no maximum set, although some maximum sets may contain them.

Examples

# A small relatedness network: two parents and their child (P1, P2, C1), a pair of
# siblings (S1, S2), three mutually related individuals (T1, T2, T3), a larger family
# (parents D1 and D2, their children K1 and K2, and K3, born to D2 and D3, a
# half-sibling of K1 and K2) and an unrelated individual (U1).
g <- igraph::graph_from_literal(P1 - C1 - P2, S1 - S2, T1 - T2 - T3 - T1,
                                D1 - K1 - D2, D1 - K2 - D2, K1 - K2,
                                D2 - K3 - D3, K1 - K3, K2 - K3, U1)
sex <- c(P1 = "F", C1 = "M", P2 = "M", S1 = "M", S2 = "F", T1 = "M", T2 = "F", T3 = "M",
         D1 = "M", K1 = "F", D2 = "F", K2 = "M", K3 = "F", D3 = "M", U1 = "F")
age <- c(P1 = 52, C1 = 21, P2 = 55, S1 = 34, S2 = 31, T1 = 60, T2 = 33, T3 = 29,
         D1 = 63, K1 = 35, D2 = 61, K2 = 38, K3 = 30, D3 = 58, U1 = 44)
igraph::V(g)$sex <- unname(sex[igraph::V(g)$name])
igraph::V(g)$age <- unname(age[igraph::V(g)$name])
sel <- rkn_select_random(g, seed = 1)
names(sel)
#>  [1] "kept"             "discarded"        "family_sizes"     "method"          
#>  [5] "uniform"          "optimal"          "criteria"         "seed"            
#>  [9] "diagnostics"      "node_diagnostics" "family_summary"   "graph"           
#> [13] "call"             "global"          
sel$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T3" "D1" "D2" "D3" "U1"
head(sel$node_diagnostics)
#>   id         pre_class post_class is_selected     pre_reason
#> 1 P1      kept_apriori       kept        TRUE  uniform_every
#> 2 C1 discarded_apriori  discarded       FALSE   uniform_none
#> 3 P2      kept_apriori       kept        TRUE  uniform_every
#> 4 S1 candidate_complex  discarded       FALSE uniform_chosen
#> 5 S2 candidate_complex       kept        TRUE uniform_chosen
#> 6 T1 candidate_complex  discarded       FALSE uniform_chosen
#>   inclusion_probability family_id family_size
#> 1             1.0000000         1           3
#> 2             0.0000000         1           3
#> 3             1.0000000         1           3
#> 4             0.5000000         2           2
#> 5             0.5000000         2           2
#> 6             0.3333333         3           3
sel$family_summary[, c("family_id", "family_size", "mis_method", "n_kept", "n_discarded")]
#>   family_id family_size mis_method n_kept n_discarded
#> 1         1           3      exact      2           1
#> 2         2           2      exact      1           1
#> 3         3           3      exact      1           2
#> 4         4           6      exact      3           3
#> 5         5           1      exact      1           0
